name: Dauphin's Violet
lede: Dauphin's Violet is a medium, blue-leaning violet from Robert Ridgway's 1912 color dictionary, named for the old French title for the heir to the throne, with no king or prince identified.

sections.title: A title, in Ridgway's person group
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 “Color Standards and Color Nomenclature” lists Dauphin's Violet at hex #725C92 among the names he credits to a person [1]. The Dauphin was the title of the heir to the French throne, used from the fourteenth century until the French monarchy ended, but Ridgway names no particular dauphin, so the exact link is undocumented in our sources [1]. The 1955 Inter-Society Color Council catalog repeats the name in the block it calls moderate purple [1].

Its nearest neighbor in our color graph is [[litho-purple|Litho Purple]], only 2.8 units away and almost the same [1]. [[blanc-s-violet|Blanc's Violet]], another Ridgway name from the same person-named group, is close behind at 3.2 units, with [[foxglove|Foxglove]] a touch further out and more vivid [1]. Against the basic color words it reads closest to [[purple|Purple]], 10.1 units off [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive matches this violet in only 0.01% of 23,781 paintings, 3 of them, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in just 1 [2]. That makes it rarer than 86% of the named colors in our set, too thin a sample for a reliable century, painter or country figure [2]. The handful of matches we do have run from 1900 to 1908, and every figure here is a computed color match in an aged photograph, not proof of a pigment or dye [2].
